# Positioning discovery

Follow [the editorial contract](../../../docs/editorial-contract.md). Use when the author asks to explore positioning, a new audience or an angle, not as a prerequisite to every draft.

1. Preserve the current mission, About page and protected language as anchors.
2. Identify the reader problem and what the author can credibly contribute from authorized evidence.
3. Offer two or three distinct angles with audience, promise, supporting evidence and trade-offs.
4. Separate hypotheses from observed audience language. Research the market only when needed and authorized; do not invent demand, differentiation or metrics.
5. Ask the author to choose, combine or reject. Record the decision privately. No exploration silently rewrites the mission or publishes a new identity.

Stop when a useful angle is selected or the remaining choice belongs to the author.
